_doc: Lanternfall's grammar extension for Lingo (docs/01 §12.4; shape docs/10 §5.11), merged into the core grammar at boot by js/talk/lingo-bridge.js — the core file is never edited. `symbols`: an intent with a core name EXTENDS it (new lines appended, each tagged; a speaker turns on its own family tag and every other family tag is zeroed), a new name is one of the 12 new intents in `meta.intents` (no more than 12), `meta.noRepeat` are the NR ones (joined to Lingo's session anti-repeat). `bind` fills a missing binding from the lexicon (pack lingo/data/packs/lanternfall.json). `defaults` are values the bridge supplies when the game did not (numbers and strings Lingo cannot bind), `aliases` rename the game's binding names (08 says dish1). `lines` are the FIXED lines by id (boss lines bl_*, Kindling hints hint_*, Marl's deal, the Narrator's first-trap and Rekindle remarks): played once as written through talk.line(id), and later replays draw from the pools above with the same tag. `voiceOf` = speak this line in another speaker's voice (the Widow's stolen voices), `fx` = voice fx override for this line, `when` = the flag that selects this variant. All text original (no third-party names). Generated 2026-09-26; edit by hand from now on.

intentDoc.odile_names_wick: Odile's comment when she tastes the wick you hold out (the NAME comes from 08's dish-name rule). Bindings flame, shape (spell entries), charm (optional).
intentDoc.pawn_recall: Hollis remembers something you sold him (memory type sold_item). Bindings item, price, days.
intentDoc.soup_menu: Brisket reads the day's menu. Bindings dish, dish2 (food entries; 08's dish1/dish2 are aliases).
intentDoc.boss_low: A boss below 25% health. Tag = the boss (tallow, gnaw, widow, bellfather, ossery).
intentDoc.idle_chatter: Hub townsfolk in passing. Tags: the act (act1..act6) and the Lamp state (lit / dark).
intentDoc.rain_talk: Anyone, about the Rain (replaces core weathertalk for this game).
intentDoc.lamp_relit: An NPC on your first visit after a relight. Binding lamp (a Great Lamp item entry).
intentDoc.ledger_arrival: The Narrator on first entry into a named place. Binding place.
intentDoc.ledger_relight: The Narrator after the fixed relight line.
intentDoc.flood_warning: Voss over the pipes. Bindings gate (a string such as "the top gate"), sec (number).
intentDoc.hush_chirr: Hush's babble gloss. Tag = trigger: wall, grapple, oil, dark, hurt, happy, scared, idle.
intentDoc.kindling_hint: A Kindling hint replayed from Chat. Tag = the flag id; the first line of each tag is the fixed hint (hint_<flag>).

odile_names_wick.t: {flame.sg} in {shape.a}. Tastes like a struck match on a cold morning.
{shape.a.cap}? Bold. I'd have braided it tighter, but I'm not the one getting bitten.
That one's got a kick like cheap brandy. I approve.
Hold it under my nose. No — closer. Ah. Wet wool and lightning.
Did you braid this in the rain? You can taste the rain.
That's a sad little wick. Feed it more oil, darling, it's starving.
Ooh. That one's going to burn somebody's eyebrows off. Possibly yours.
It tastes like the Lamp did, when I was a girl.
Too much {charm.or(charm)}. Like salt in tea. Still, you'll drink it.

pawn_recall.t: You sold me {item.a} for {price} pennies. I sold it for four times that. Just so you know.
Still miss that {item.sg}? I don't. Found a good home. Mine.
Last time you were here you practically gave me {item.a}. Do it again, would you?
{days, plural, one{Yesterday} other{# days ago}}, {item.a}. You're a creature of habit.
That {item.sg} you pawned? A drowned fellow tried to buy it. Tried.
I've got your {item.sg} in the back. Want it? Twice the price. Sentiment's extra.
You don't haggle like somebody who sold {item.a} for {price}.
I keep a book. You're in it. Several pages.
Selling again? Your {item.sg} was the last thing I bought that didn't leak.
The {item.sg}. Yes. I remember your face when you let it go. Priceless. Well — {price} pennies.
Every time you walk in I think, what's this one going to cost me? Then I remember: nothing, it's you.

soup_menu.t: Today it's {dish.sg} and {dish2.sg}. Or the mystery bowl, if you're feeling lucky.
{dish.sg.cap}, fresh as it gets down here, which isn't very.
I've got {dish.sg}. Don't make that face, it's good for you.
Mystery bowl's bubbling. It bubbled back at me earlier. Your call.
The eels were biting this morning. Well. The eels were biting me. Either way, {dish.sg}.
You look thin. Two bowls. No, I'm not charging for the second. Yes I am.
There's {dish.sg} for the brave and {dish2.sg} for the sensible.
Don't ask what's in the mystery bowl. I don't ask it either.
Hot soup, cold rain, that's the whole of wisdom.
I'd do you a pie, but the oven's underwater again.
Last one who skipped supper went down the Brickgut and came back a rat. Eat.

boss_low.t: So warm. Why is it so warm.
I was a statue. I was only a statue.
[The Choir falters. One voice keeps singing.]
[Saint Gnaw screams a note no rat can hold.]
Let it go out. Let it all go out.
One more day. I only wanted one more day.
I can't remember how to open my hand.

idle_chatter.t: Lamp's flickering again.
Candles cost a week's wage now.
My gran says the Stair used to be warm.
Did you see it flare? Whole street cheered.
Wax is setting nice and hard now.
I slept a whole night.
Hear the singing? Don't listen.
Rats took the Pottle boy's boots. With him in them.
Keep to the chains.
Rats won't come in the light. Can you believe it.
Market stays open past dark now. Past dark!
Smell that? Somebody is frying something.
Top gate first. Everybody knows.
The water's warm now. Warm.
I saw the Pale singing under the gauge tower.
Don't whistle in the dark.
Oil's cheaper if you don't ask where from.
Light your lamp and they come. Put it out and they wait.
The bells stopped. Doesn't feel right.
My feet keep wanting to go up.
Tithe-folk aren't all bad. Just most.
Is that — is that a star?
It's so quiet. I hate it. I love it.
Forty years of rain in my boots.

rain_talk.t: Forty years. You'd think it'd get tired.
My roof has more holes than roof.
My mother says she remembers dry. I think she's making it up.
It's not raining harder. You're just deeper.
Rain's got a sound down here. Like somebody breathing.
Don't drink it. Well. Don't drink it much.
I've stopped owning dry socks. It's freeing, in a way.
It rained on my wedding. It rained on my christening. It'll rain on my funeral, I expect.
Some nights I swear it's crying.
When it stops — if — what'll we even talk about?
Rain keeps the dust down. That's the one good thing. I've been looking for forty years.
The Cloudwardens did this. Don't say that too loud.

lamp_relit.t: You did it. You actually lit {lamp.the}.
I cried. Don't tell anybody. I cried.
{lamp.sg.cap}! My kids had never seen it lit.
The whole tier's warm. I'd forgotten warm.
They'll write you in the Ledger for that.
I thought it was a story. {lamp.sg.cap}, lit. Look at it.
Took you long enough. Thank you. Took you long enough.
I can see my hands. Isn't that silly? I can see my hands.
How many more? Don't tell me. Just go light them.
Some of the old folk went down to the rail just to stare at it.
Every window on the Face lit up at once. Like the Face was smiling.
I'll never complain about the lamp tax again. Probably.

ledger_arrival.t: {place.sg.cap}. The Ledger has no entry here for forty years.
{place.sg.cap}. Somebody lived here. Somebody left in a hurry.
{place.sg.cap}. A lamp-hook on every wall, and no lamps.
{place.sg.cap}. The air smells of old oil.
{place.sg.cap}. Nothing moves. Nothing that wants to be seen.
{place.sg.cap}. The last Lamplighter's mark on the lintel is thirty years old.
{place.sg.cap}. Even the dark here is damp.
{place.sg.cap}, where the city went to be forgotten.
{place.sg.cap}. Something has been eating the candles.
{place.sg.cap}. The Ledger opens a new page.

ledger_relight.t: Somewhere above, somebody opens a window.
The water catches the colour and holds it.
The rain goes on. It looks different now.
One more light in the Hollow.
The dark steps back. Not far.
Children who have never seen the colour are looking at it now.
The old brass remembers its work.
Forty years of dark, and it took one wick.
A gutter that has run black for years runs gold for a minute.
On every tier, someone stops and looks up.

flood_warning.t: Top gate first! Always the top gate first!
It's filling — you've got {sec}, maybe less.
Don't touch the red wheel! The other red wheel!
The Maw's coming up with the water — get off the floor!
Close {gate.sg}! Close it or you'll drown the lot of us!
Hear that groan? That's the gate. Move.
Level's dropping. Now's your chance, go go go!
Twenty-eight years I've watched that gauge. It's never been that high.

kindling_hint.t: She was only ever cold. If you must put her out — put her out with something cold. Please.
Cold, not cruel. That's all I ask.
Rime or the water. Not fire. She's had enough fire.
That sweep girl follows you like a moth. Give her something to carry and she'll carry it for life.
The sweep wants a lantern post. Let her carry one.
Trust that child with something heavy. She'll grow into it.
My brother went down the rat pipes with a lantern. Never pawned it. Never came back up with it either.
Abel's lantern is still down there somewhere. Not that I care.
A brass lantern with a crane on the lid isn't for sale. If you find it, bring it here.
If the dry ones open the valve, we go out with the water. Leave it, dry one. Leave it shut.
The valve stays shut, dry one. Please.
Drain our market and we drain with it.
Nell went into Stilt Town on her own. Stubborn girl. Somebody ought to go after her before it's too late.
Nell's out in Stilt Town. Alone. That girl.
Take her a bowl, and take her home, if you can.
If you finish her, finish her in gold light. She always wanted to see it once more.
Gold light, at the end. That's all she'd want.
Don't finish my sister in the dark. Please.
The Knell kneel, if you let them. Folk down here remember who let them get back up.
A Knell on his knees is still a man.
Let one walk away and see who remembers.
Something in the root still carries a lantern. I see it glow at night, halfway up.
There is a lantern in the root. It never goes out.
Halfway up the root, a light. Somebody's still keeping it.

enemy_opener.t: Kneel, and fall the right way!
Your light is a noise. We are the only noise.
Fall with us, it's so much easier.
Put it out and walk away.
The water's warm, if you wait long enough.
Put the light out, it stings.

combat_bark.t: Hear it? That's your end ringing!

combat_flee.t: I'll go. I'll go, just let me go.
Don't — I've a sister in the Tithe Hall!
The Toll can have me later. Not today.
Take the bell. Take it, I don't want it.
I never liked the dark anyway.

combat_taunt.t: Every step down is a step closer to the Toll.
Kneel now and it won't hurt.
Hear that? Your little light is shaking.
The dark is patient. So are we.
Put it out yourself. Save us the trouble.
You fall like a proper bell.
Sink a little. Just a little.

combat_hurt.t: It rings — it rings in my teeth!

combat_kill.t: Rest. It will rain on you, too, for a while.
Another candle out. I am sorry.

beast_snarl.t: [Squeaking, in harmony. It's worse in harmony.]
["Saint, saint, saint," the rats seem to say.]
[One rat sings off-key. The others turn on it.]
[Tiny claws keep time on the pipes.]
[The swarm sings the note the Lamp used to hum.]
[A high thin descant from the ceiling.]
[They're singing your footsteps back to you.]
[A child's voice that isn't: "come play in the dark."]
[The whisper stops when your lantern flares.]
[Something drips from the ceiling, and it's talking.]
["We were lamplighters too," says the dark.]

named_beast.t: The Sluicemaw circles, and the water follows.
Something the size of a barge turns under the surface.
The gauges jump. The Maw is rising.
The reservoir heaves, and a mouth opens in it.

boss_opener.t: Little wick. Come in out of the rain.
They fed me nine years of candles. I'm still so cold.
[Saint Gnaw raises a claw; the swarm falls silent.]
[The Choir hums a note you feel in your teeth.]
Put the lamp down. You're safe now.
I loved the light more than anyone.
Forty years, and they send a child with a candle.
Do you know what a dry sky looked like? I don't. Not anymore.

boss_phase.t: You're hurting me. I'll hold you tighter.
I'm melting — I'm melting into you.
Every drop of me will find you.
Dark, dark, dark — isn't it restful?
You've lit their Lamps. You think that makes it day?
Elsbet hated the rain. I keep it for her. I keep it.
Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing.
You took the Lamplighter out of my root. He was good company.

last_words.t: The wick's gone out. Oh, that's nicer.
So cool. So quiet. Thank you, little wick.
[The Choir falters. One voice keeps singing, then stops.]
[A single squeak, and then the pipes are quiet.]
Oh. That's what it looked like.

greet.t: Evening. It's always evening down here.
Oil in the lamp, I see. Good.
Come in out of the rain, {listener.name}.

farewell.t: Don't let the rain in your lantern.
Go on, then. The dark's waiting.

warning.t: Mind the edge — it's a long drop!
Your light — keep your light up!

relief.t: The dark backed off. For now.

fear.t: Don't let the light go out.
It's too dark. It's far too dark.
The lamp's shaking. Is it the lamp or me?
What if it never stops raining?

thanks.t: I'll remember that when the lamps are lit.
Thank you. Truly. Mind the oil.
You've got a good light in you.
That's a kindness I won't forget.

trade_haggle.t: You want it cheap, go and find it in a flood.
I'll knock off a penny. One.
Price goes down when the Lamp goes up.

trade_refuse.t: Not for that price. Not in this rain.
Come back when your purse is heavier.
No. And don't drip on the counter.
That's not money, that's a puddle.

pray.t: Keep the wick dry, keep the flame true.
By the old oil and the new light.
Let the Rain pass over us.

observe.t: Wax on the floor. Somebody came this way.
The water's higher than last time.
Old oil. You can smell it.
Soot on the walls — something burned here.
That drip's been going forty years.

bl_tallow_open.speaker: boss_tallow
bl_tallow_open.text: Little wick. Come in out of the rain.

bl_tallow_p1.speaker: boss_tallow
bl_tallow_p1.text: They fed me nine years of candles. I'm still so cold.

bl_tallow_p2.speaker: boss_tallow
bl_tallow_p2.text: You're hurting me. I'll hold you tighter.

bl_tallow_p3.speaker: boss_tallow
bl_tallow_p3.text: I'm melting — I'm melting into you.

bl_gnaw_p1.speaker: boss_gnaw
bl_gnaw_p1.text: [Saint Gnaw raises a claw; the swarm falls silent.]

bl_gnaw_death.speaker: boss_gnaw
bl_gnaw_death.text: [The Choir falters. One voice keeps singing, then stops.]

bl_sluicemaw_open.speaker: narrator
bl_sluicemaw_open.text: The Sluicemaw rolls in the dark water, and the gauges on the wall all jump at once.

bl_sluicemaw_p1.speaker: narrator
bl_sluicemaw_p1.text: It circles. The water circles with it.

bl_sluicemaw_p2.speaker: narrator
bl_sluicemaw_p2.text: The reservoir drops, and the Maw goes down with it, hungry.

bl_sluicemaw_p3.speaker: narrator
bl_sluicemaw_p3.text: Every gate in the Ward groans at once.

bl_sluicemaw_death.speaker: narrator
bl_sluicemaw_death.text: The Sluicemaw sinks. For the first time in twenty-eight years, the gauges read still.

bl_widow_p1.speaker: boss_widow
bl_widow_p1.text: Put the lamp down. You're safe now.

bl_ossery_open.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_open.text: Forty years, and they send a child with a candle.

bl_ossery_p2.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_p2.text: You've lit their Lamps. You think that makes it day?

bl_ossery_p3.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_p3.text: Elsbet hated the rain. I keep it for her. I keep it.

bl_ossery_p4.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_p4.text: Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing. I had forgotten what nothing sounded like.

bl_ossery_freeze.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_freeze.text: One more day. I only wanted one more day.

bl_ossery_refuse.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_refuse.text: You don't know what it's like to let go.

bl_ossery_kill.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_kill.text: Rest. It will rain on you, too, for a while.

bl_tallow_death_cooled.speaker: boss_tallow
bl_tallow_death_cooled.text: So cool. So quiet. Thank you, little wick.

bl_widow_death_gleam.speaker: boss_widow
bl_widow_death_gleam.text: Oh. That's what it looked like.

bl_ossery_p2_corvin.speaker: boss_ossery
bl_ossery_p2_corvin.text: You took the Lamplighter out of my root. He was good company.

hint_tallow_cooled.speaker: npc_seld
hint_tallow_cooled.text: She was only ever cold. If you must put her out — put her out with something cold. Please.

hint_pim_trusted.speaker: npc_aldra
hint_pim_trusted.text: That sweep girl follows you like a moth. Give her something to carry and she'll carry it for life.

hint_hollis_lantern.speaker: npc_hollis
hint_hollis_lantern.text: My brother went down the rat pipes with a lantern. Never pawned it. Never came back up with it either.

hint_pale_kept.speaker: npc_unna
hint_pale_kept.text: If the dry ones open the valve, we go out with the water. Leave it, dry one. Leave it shut.

hint_nell_alive.speaker: npc_brisket
hint_nell_alive.text: Nell went into Stilt Town on her own. Stubborn girl. Somebody ought to go after her before it's too late.

hint_widow_mercy.speaker: npc_mothwife
hint_widow_mercy.text: If you finish her, finish her in gold light. She always wanted to see it once more.

hint_knell_spared.speaker: npc_wenna
hint_knell_spared.text: The Knell kneel, if you let them. Folk down here remember who let them get back up.

hint_corvin_freed.speaker: npc_merrit
hint_corvin_freed.text: Something in the root still carries a lantern. I see it glow at night, halfway up.

marl_deal_named.speaker: npc_marl
marl_deal_named.text: Ten of mine have walked away from you. Make it ten, Lamplighter, and I'll call you a friend of the Toll.

marl_deal_5.speaker: npc_marl
marl_deal_5.text: Five of mine walked home last week and swore a Lamplighter let them. Five. The flock is counting, child.

marl_deal_9.speaker: npc_marl
marl_deal_9.text: Nine. One more, and the Tithe Hall rings for you instead of against you.

nr_first_trap_kill.speaker: narrator
nr_first_trap_kill.text: Entered in the Ledger, under The Hollow: one enemy, killed by the city itself. The city approves.

nr_rekindle_1.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_1.text: Entered in the Ledger: a room, put back. The Ledger has seen worse.

nr_rekindle_2.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_2.text: The wax remembers. So does the Ledger.

nr_rekindle_4.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_4.text: The Ledger turns back a page. Only one.

nr_rekindle_5.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_5.text: Put right. The rain did not notice.

nr_rekindle_7.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_7.text: A room, as it was. You, as you are.

nr_rekindle_8.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_8.text: The Ledger does not judge. It only counts.

nr_rekindle_9.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_9.text: Every stone back where it fell from. Mostly.

nr_rekindle_10.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_10.text: Rekindled. Try the other way this time.

nr_rekindle_11.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_11.text: The city resets its trap. Politely.

nr_rekindle_12.speaker: narrator
nr_rekindle_12.text: Entered twice. The second entry is shorter.
